clinician.trajectory_summary: A 20-year-old man with a history of right tibial osteosarcoma and recent brain and lung metastases presented with decreased vision in his right eye and a large, posterior pole, pink, nodular, subretinal mass. Imaging (MRI, A/B-scan ultrasonography, CT) characterized the mass as a heterogeneous choroidal lesion. At one-month follow-up, the eye was painful with a detached retina and elevated intraocular pressure. The ocular lesion subsequently responded to systemic treatment, decreasing in volume according to CT and MRI scans, supporting the diagnosis of choroidal osteosarcoma metastasis.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Patient presented with decreased vision in the right eye and a subretinal mass.
Patient has a history of right tibial osteosarcoma diagnosed at age 17, treated with supracondylar amputation, and recent diagnosis of brain and lung metastases.
Ophthalmic examination revealed a large, posterior pole, pink, nodular, subretinal mass, with associated fluid in the right eye.
MRI showed a well-defined, irregular choroidal mass, T1-isointense and T2-hypointense.

A and B-scan ultrasonography confirmed a subretinal, heterogeneous mass with medium/high reflectivity, areas of localized increased and decreased reflectivity, and a height-to-base ratio (HBR) of 1-1.2.
CT revealed a heterogeneous, well-defined mass within the uveal layer, hyperdense, with areas of decreased density, significant intraocular involvement, and contrast-enhancement.
The ocular lesion responded to systemic treatment and decreased in volume, according to CT and MRI scans.

ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.basis: The patient's known history of widespread metastatic osteosarcoma and the ocular lesion's response to systemic treatment make a primary ocular tumor less likely.

remaining_uncertainties: Histopathological confirmation of the choroidal mass was not obtained.
Specific details of the systemic treatment administered were not reported.
